plain_description.what: When a judge model agrees more with a better reference answer, the gain was split into two parts: agreeing because both are right, and agreeing because both are wrong in the same way. Only the both-wrong part was compared with the spread across models.
plain_description.why: It asks whether conditioning on correctness can separate 'agrees because right' from 'agrees because the models make correlated errors'.
plain_description.information: Result (no new calls): undetermined. Every interval contains zero, and the verdict depends on the reading. The conditional version is as tied to reference accuracy as the plain one. On the both-wrong questions, the models mostly converge on the same wrong option. The plan to use this conditional gate should not proceed. It is on older judged data now ruled history.
